articles.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
articles.summary: Claims the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 sandpaper cheating plot are dividing the cricket world.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
articles.summaryTr: Claims the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 sandpaper cheating plot are dividing the cricket world.
articles.articleText: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' - Published As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. And there's a sense of injustice that Australia can't seem to escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. In it, he said he had wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the tampering after batsman Cameron Bancroft was caught with the sandpaper on field. "I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'." However Khawaja has since said he didn't want to start a "witch hunt" and has refused to answer questions on exactly who he claims knew of the scheme, and what they knew. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja had written the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve Smith, the captain at the time who was also suspended, has been travelling overseas and is yet to say anything publicly about the claims in the book. Bancroft is also staying silent for now despite previously suggesting the bowlers knew. But half of Australia's living cricket royalty and a slew of former coaches - some of whom have been accused of wrongdoing too - have thrown in their two cents. And Cricket Australia is under pressure from some to reopen its investigation into sandpapergate - something chief executive Todd Greenberg has already ruled out. Prof David Rowe of the University of Western Sydney told the BBC the saga was still so painful for many players and fans as the country sees itself as "a nation of good sports". "The idea of being a good sport is two things. One is being good at sport, so you actually win. But the other side is that you do it honourably and fairly," he said. "Many Australians would see themselves as above all that. That is: cheating is what other teams get up to... not the nation of good sports." He said the revelation was a "nasty shock" which brought the country "collective shame" which lingers today. He says he doubts that the cricket scene would be able to move on without a fresh response from the governing body, Cricket Australia. "One of the best ways to fuel conspiracy theories and keep sandpapergate going is to essentially say 'there's no more to see here' - especially when that comes from the authorities," Rowe said. Asked about a fresh investigation, Cummins said it was a matter for Cricket Australia. Over the marathon press conference - which one reporter suggested was the longest in Australian sporting history - Cummins was cautious, pausing often to consider his responses and to make sure they answered the questions being asked of him. But he was also frank - using strong words to reject what he said were "vague" claims by Khawaja and admitting he was frustrated a friend had put him in this position. "Friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations... That's something I've been grappling with the last couple of days." As the reporters ran out of steam, Cummins said it was "annoying" that sandpapergate scandal was still a distraction for Australian cricket. He gestured outside to the Sheffield Shield match and mentioned Friday's one-day international against England in Perth, from which he and other key players are being rested. "It's been eight years... Hopefully today we put a line through it and we're done and we can all move on to much more fun topics, like actual cricket." Few people think he'll get his wish. "It's going to be hard to move on, given that there's two sides of the story and it doesn't look like either side is going to back down," James said. "I don't know what the outcome will be." articles.title: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
articles.summary: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
articles.summaryTr: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.
articles.articleText: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite - Published Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall and several other contestants from Africa could miss this year's competition in Puerto Rico as they race to secure a US visa. Hall is due to represent Zimbabwe at the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, with the winner set to be crowned on 24 November. But she has yet to obtain a visa to travel to the US territory. "We have been back and forth, trying to get my visa approved," Hall said in a video posted on her Instagram page. Hall is not the only African contestant to be affected by the restrictions. Zambia has withdrawn its representative, Pamela Mubanga, from the competition because of US travel restrictions. Contestants began arriving in Puerto Rico on 8 November for registration, fittings and other pre-pageant activities, putting pressure on Hall, and others including the representative from South Sudan, to secure their visas. "Officially, today is the day I was supposed to be leaving for Puerto Rico for the 75th edition of Miss Universe," Hall said. Zimbabwe is among 19 countries subject to partial US travel restrictions introduced under the Presidential Proclamation 10998, which took effect on 1 January 2026. The measures suspend the issuance of visitor, student and exchange visas, as well as immigrant visas, to nationals of the affected countries. They also impose restrictions on other categories of non-immigrant visas. In a statement, the Miss Universe organization in Zambia said Mubanga's situation was a consequence of the travel restrictions rather than individual circumstances. "Unlike situations where a contestant's visa is denied due to personal circumstances, documentation or organisational challenges, Mubanga's situation is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction affecting Zambia and other African countries," the statement read. Mubanga, 25, a registered nurse, was crowned Miss Universe Zambia on 8 October and was due to represent the country at the international pageant. The statement said five other African countries faced similar difficulties, although it did not name them. Hall said she shared their concerns, adding that she had spent the past few weeks in South Africa trying to secure her visa. "I am not alone in this predicament. Some of my African sisters are facing the same predicament, and I know exactly what they are going through," she said. Miss Universe South Sudan also expressed uncertainty about her participation, commenting on Hall's video: "It is 50/50 whether we will make it, Miss Universe." In another video posted three days earlier, Hall said she was still hoping to make it to Puerto Rico. She captioned the video: "The fight to get Zimbabwe to Puerto Rico continues," The pageant's final is scheduled to take place at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan. articles.title: Politicians back focus on cost of living
articles.summary: The Government of Jersey's key priorities are passed despite concerns over a lack of "real action".

articles.titleTr: Politicians back focus on cost of living
articles.summaryTr: The Government of Jersey's key priorities are passed despite concerns over a lack of "real action".
articles.articleText: Politicians back focus on cost of living - Published Politicians have backed the Government of Jersey's key priorities for the next political term which includes action on the cost of living. States members adopted the Common Strategic Policy, external which lays out the Council of Ministers' priorities for the political term until 2030. The priorities are centered around four pillars including targeted action on the cost of living, restoring Jersey's competitiveness, investing in homes and infrastructure and maintaining financial stability. Chief Minister Lyndon Farnham said the government was determined "to make Jersey a more affordable place to live" but Reform Jersey co-leader Lyndsay Feltham said the policy lacked "real action". The policy was backed with 31 votes in favour, 10 against and two abstentions. Ministers first published the proposed policy in September and this week politicians debated a number of amendments proposed by backbenchers. This included adding a priority about government transparency and promoting democracy, bringing the total number of priorities up from 11 to 12. Deputy Feltham's amendments to add actions to the policy about household affordability and employment rights were rejected and members also voted not to include reference to rental stress. The Reform Jersey co-leader said she was worried about the gaps this left behind. "What I really wanted to see from government was something more sustained and a sustained commitment to reduce everyday cost of living," said Feltham. "They've committed to a review of household affordability. A review doesn't put food on the table or a roof over somebody's head. "I am really concerned that ministers aren't going to actually take any action." However, the chief minister said the policy recognised islanders' concerns such as affordability, housing, economic growth, investing in infrastructure and protecting the environment. In his closing speech, Farnham said their contributions "reflected a shared commitment to securing the best possible future for our island". He said the policy "will send an important message to islanders that we are putting their interests before our political disagreements". articles.title: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow
articles.summary: Producers claimed without more support, they could be forced to stop using British-grown apples.

articles.titleTr: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow
articles.summaryTr: Producers claimed without more support, they could be forced to stop using British-grown apples.
articles.articleText: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow - Published Rising costs could force the cider industry to reduce their reliance on British-grown apples, according to several well-established businesses. Higher alcohol duty, energy bills and packaging costs are making it harder to stay profitable, according to a producer in Somerset. The government said it was supporting the sector by increasing the value of Small Producer Relief, which provides lower alcohol duty rates for some smaller and medium-sized producers. Matilda Temperley, director of Burrow Hill farm near Martock, said it would be a "tragedy" to stop using its own apples due to climbing costs. Temperley, whose farm has been growing apples for 300 years, said recent increases had added to pressures already facing the industry, adding at 6% alcohol, their traditional cider is taxed at a higher rate than mass produced cider. More from Somerset - Christmas market fears as roadworks cause long delays - Published6 hours ago - Gritters out for the first time this autumn - Published20 hours ago - No radical change after nationalisation, GWR says - Published16 hours ago "By next February, we will have seen a 61% increase in tax on our standard 50cl bottles," Temperley claimed. She welcomed the rise in Small Producers Relief but said other mounting costs outweighed it. "We've got huge, energy costs, then almost a 90% increase in tax costs since 2020." "The thing that will happen is that if you're a big cider maker, you're going to look to cut your costs and the only way to cut costs is to stop using British apples," she said. "That's a real tragedy because cider should be made from these beautiful orchards". Isaac Stell, a financial analyst at Wealth Club in Bristol, said that having pledged not to raise the main rates of income tax, national insurance or VAT for working people, the recent budget focused on other areas to "help plug the fiscal hole." He said producers were also dealing with higher employer National Insurance contributions and increases in the minimum wage. "Inevitably, some of those additional costs will find their way through to the pubs, clubs and restaurants that producers supply, and ultimately to an already squeezed consumer. " The Showerings family, known for producing Babycham, has been making drinks in Shepton Mallet for more than 14 generations. "Our business has grown a lot in the last ten years - we've gone from having 80 employees to around 350 now," the firm's managing director Matthew Showering said. "We've had a good couple of years, we're making drinks that are popular and growing." While acknowledging rising costs, Showering said he would rather see less government intervention. "We don't want any help from the government, we'd rather they keep out of things as much as possible." Matt Gillett from Tricky's Cider in Low Ham said the size of his operation means he will be eligible for the Small Producer Relief but adds he will not see a huge benefit as the Alcohol Duty is a "fairly substantial" part of his monthly outgoings. Gillett remains optimistic, and said he would not consider importing pulp or concentrate to cut costs. "We are a craft producer here in Somerset and are proud of the fact we take from local orchards, traditional orchards, and use the fruit that is available here in this county." A spokesperson for the Treasury said: "The cider industry makes a vital contribution to our rural economy and communities, and cider continues to benefit from significantly lower duty rates than other alcoholic drinks. "But we know the industry is facing continued pressures, which is why the Budget provides additional support by cutting costs for pubs and bars that are vital customers for the industry and poured pints continue to benefit from draught relief." articles.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, US President Donald Trump nominated four new SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for prominent crypto advocate Hester Peirce; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang abruptly resigned as the chipmaker’s shares plunged and a Coinbase executive warned that proposed EU restrictions on decentralized finance could push users toward riskier platforms. Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO and stepped down from the company’s board on Thursday, effective immediately. The board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Kress will retain her role as CFO while Nvidia’s board considers internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones its first chair and said it expects Nvidia’s operations to proceed without interruption. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Bitcoin (BTC) fell alongside Nvidia shares, dropping as much as 3.5% to a multimonth low. The shares later pared losses to trade at $165 at 4:24 p.m. UTC, down 5% on the day. The stock was down more than 26% over the previous month. EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec European Union efforts to tighten oversight of decentralized finance (DeFi) could drive crypto users toward platforms offering fewer investor protections, according to Coinbase’s head of EU policy. Roeland Van der Stappen told Cointelegraph that regulated crypto platforms could respond by limiting or dropping access to DeFi services. “Rules designed to protect investors would end up pushing activity towards the places with the least protection,” Van der Stappen said. In its September response to the European Commission’s consultation on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the European Securities and Markets Authority recommended creating a new category of regulated crypto services for firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols.

articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summary: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.

articles.titleTr: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.summaryTr: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
articles.articleText: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. - How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions - Published19 hours ago - The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published19 hours ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. - Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? - Published21 hours ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia. Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago. Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector. articles.titleTr: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
articles.summaryTr: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
articles.articleText: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say - Published Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision. Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her". John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed". They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said. He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time". In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

articles.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
articles.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

articles.titleTr: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
articles.summaryTr: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
articles.articleText: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI - Published State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

articles.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summary: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.

news.titleTr: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summaryTr: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
news.articleText: What we know about the global Microsoft outage - Published A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products. Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems". Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues. How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening. The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting. Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected. From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread. Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed. In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected. The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted. Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage. Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report. What has Microsoft said? Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure. The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do. In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these. On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added it is focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" and warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue". In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected". What have experts said? Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Paul Spain from New Zealand-based advisory firm Gorilla Technology said that with e-mails and services offline, companies have practically "lost a business day", which is "frustrating" users". news.articleText: Selim Güven CNBC-e'ye konuştu: ACWA'dan Türkiye'ye 5-6 milyar doları aşan yatırım hedefi - ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, Türkiye'deki yatırım kapasitesini yenilenebilir enerji, batarya depolama ve iletim sistemleriyle 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkarmayı hedeflediklerini açıkladı. Güven, 1,6 milyar euroluk ilk faz projesinin temelinin mart-nisan döneminde atılacağını bildirdi. ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, COP31 Zirvesi kapsamında CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle COP31'in şirket açısından önemine değinen Güven, ACWA'nın yaklaşık 16 ülkede aktif olarak bulunduğunu ve farklı ülkelere de girmek istediklerini söyledi. Uluslararası bir organizasyon olan COP31'in yaklaşık 196 ülkeyi bir araya getirdiğini belirten Güven, "Böyle bir organizasyon, hem paydaşlarımızla hem de potansiyel müşterilerimizle, ülkelerle, tedarikçilerle ve ortaklarımızla bir araya gelip anlaşmalar yapma, projelerimizi değerlendirme ve tekrar bağlantımızı kurma açısından çok önemli." diye konuştu. Güven, COP31'in bu yıl "uygulama COP'u" olarak tanımlanmasının da önem taşıdığını ifade ederek, "Projelerin kağıttan artık yapılabilir, inşa edilebilir, finanse edilebilir gerçek projelere dönüşmesi hedefiyle çok önemli bir organizasyon." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. "Mart-nisan döneminde projenin temelini atacağız" Türkiye'deki yatırım planlarının ilk fazına ilişkin bilgi veren Güven, geçen mart ayında gerçekleştirilen görüşmede de ilk fazın başladığını, sahaların hükümetler arası anlaşma kapsamında belirlendiğini ve tarifenin de karara bağlandığını hatırlattı. O dönemde yaklaşık bir yıl içinde temel atma çalışmalarına başlayacaklarını söylediklerini aktaran Güven, planın sürdüğünü bildirdi. Güven, şu anda teknik, hukuki, finansman, çevre ve sosyal alanlarda yoğun çalışmaların devam ettiğini belirterek, şunları kaydetti: "Attığımız imza da bunun çok önemli bir adımını oluşturuyor. Bankaların bu projeye ilişkin taahhütlerini belirleyen bir anlaşma imzaladık. İnşallah mart-nisan ayında da bu projenin temelini atacağız." Söz konusu projenin 1,6 milyar euro büyüklüğünde olduğunu vurgulayan Güven, uluslararası önemli yatırım bankalarından 9'unun projeye kredi veren olarak katılma taahhütlerini içeren imza töreninin gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. Güven, anlaşmanın projenin önemli bir evreye girdiğini ve planlandığı şekilde ilerlediğini gösterdiğini belirterek, "Aynı zamanda projemizin teknik ve diğer yatırımcı planı, çevre, sosyal, teknik ve hukuki incelemelerinin de belli bir aşamayı geçtiğinin göstergesi." ifadelerini kullandı. Anlaşmanın Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji stratejisine ve ülkeye duyulan güvene işaret eden önemli bir aşama olduğunu dile getiren Güven, projenin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarından destek almasının önemine dikkati çekti. "Yatırım kapasitemizi 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkaracağız" ACWA'nın Türkiye'deki yatırım planının ilk fazın ardından da devam edeceğini bildiren Güven, daha önce açıkladıkları 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımına iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de eklemeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi. Güven, "Hedefimiz, buradaki daha önce de konuştuğumuz 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımını ve üstüne iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de ekleyerek yatırımı daha da büyütmek. Böylece yatırımımızı yaklaşık 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkacak bir yatırım kapasitesine ulaştıracağız." dedi. Yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının yanı sıra depolama sistemleri ve iletim altyapısının da önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Güven, şöyle devam etti: "Öncelikle, dünyada küresel olarak Türkiye örneğinin dışında da aynı konu söz konusu. Yenilenebilir enerji yatırımları bir problemin bir konusu. Diğer konusu depolamalar çünkü esnekliğinizi ve 24 saat enerji tedarikini kesintisiz verebilmenizi sağlıyor. Biliyorsunuz, yenilenebilir enerjinin daha önceden hep ders kitaplarında söylenilen kesintili olması, rüzgarın ve güneşin kesintili olması konusu var. Depolamalı sistemlerle bu kesinti problemini çözüyorsunuz. 24 saate kadar depolamalarla bu sorunu çözerek kesintisiz elektrik sağlayabiliyorsunuz." Küresel ölçekte bir diğer önemli sorunun iletim altyapısı olduğuna işaret eden Güven, iletim sistemlerine yönelik yatırımların geride kaldığını belirtti. Güven, 1,6 milyar euroluk ilk faz projesinin temelinin mart-nisan döneminde atılacağını bildirdi. ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, COP31 Zirvesi kapsamında CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle COP31'in şirket açısından önemine değinen Güven, ACWA'nın yaklaşık 16 ülkede aktif olarak bulunduğunu ve farklı ülkelere de girmek istediklerini söyledi. Uluslararası bir organizasyon olan COP31'in yaklaşık 196 ülkeyi bir araya getirdiğini belirten Güven, "Böyle bir organizasyon, hem paydaşlarımızla hem de potansiyel müşterilerimizle, ülkelerle, tedarikçilerle ve ortaklarımızla bir araya gelip anlaşmalar yapma, projelerimizi değerlendirme ve tekrar bağlantımızı kurma açısından çok önemli." diye konuştu. Güven, COP31'in bu yıl "uygulama COP'u" olarak tanımlanmasının da önem taşıdığını ifade ederek, "Projelerin kağıttan artık yapılabilir, inşa edilebilir, finanse edilebilir gerçek projelere dönüşmesi hedefiyle çok önemli bir organizasyon." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. news.titleTr: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
news.summaryTr: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.
news.articleText: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House - Published How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. But that relationship now looks rather more complicated. The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department. This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle. Now the political pressure is building. Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach. And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure. Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open. Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors. The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment. It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history". That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out. There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long? The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump. The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns. This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department. Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology? - Published21 hours ago

news.summaryTr: Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts.
news.articleText: Israeli police arrest five in $5M WhatsApp crypto trading probe Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts. Israeli police arrested five people on Tuesday in a money laundering investigation involving about 16 million shekels ($5 million) in crypto transactions arranged through a WhatsApp group. Investigators from the National Unit for Combating Economic Crime within Lahav 433 suspect the group provided crypto services without a license and failed to report transactions to Israel’s tax authorities. Police allege the group used fictitious agreements to make crypto proceeds transferred into bank accounts look like loans, according to The Jerusalem Post. Authorities seized wallets, computers and tens of thousands of shekels in cash while searching the suspects’ homes. Investigators questioned the five on suspicion of money laundering, fraud and providing financial asset services without a license. Israel’s Tax Authority announced two other arrests on Oct. 6 in cases involving suspected failures to report crypto activity. One involved trades worth tens of millions of dollars. In the other, an Ashdod resident allegedly failed to report income from about $13 million in crypto trades between 2019 and 2021. A November 2024 audit by Israel’s State Comptroller found that about 500 people reported crypto activity each year on average from 2018 to 2022, out of at least 200,000 potential filers. Related: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam

news.titleTr: QNB Türkiye'den 500 milyon dolarlık sürdürülebilir finansman anlaşması
news.summaryTr: QNB Türkiye Genel Müdürü Ömür Tan, 5 yıl vadeli 500 milyon dolarlık sürdürülebilir finansmanın yeşil dönüşüm, elektrifikasyon, kadın istihdamı ve deprem bölgesi ile yatırım öncelikli bölgelerdeki KOBİ'lerin gelişimi için kullanılacağını açıkladı.
news.articleText: QNB Türkiye'den 500 milyon dolarlık sürdürülebilir finansman anlaşması - QNB Türkiye Genel Müdürü Ömür Tan, 5 yıl vadeli 500 milyon dolarlık sürdürülebilir finansmanın yeşil dönüşüm, elektrifikasyon, kadın istihdamı ve deprem bölgesi ile yatırım öncelikli bölgelerdeki KOBİ'lerin gelişimi için kullanılacağını açıkladı. QNB Türkiye Genel Müdürü Ömür Tan, COP31 Zirvesi kapsamında CNBC-e muhabiri Tanem Zaman'ın sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Zirvenin son yıllardaki en üst düzey katılımın gerçekleştiği COP organizasyonlarından biri olduğunu belirten Tan, bu COP'un önceki zirvelerden en önemli farkının taahhütlerden uygulamaya geçiş olduğunu ifade etti. Tan, "Açıkçası çok yoğun geçtiğini söyleyebilirim. Son yıllardaki en üst düzey katılımın olduğu, en yoğun katılımın olduğu COP olduğu söyleniyor. Biz de burada bunu birebir takip ediyoruz. Yaklaşık 4 gündür buradayız. Çok yoğun geçiyor. Tabii bu COP'un genel olarak diğer COP'lardan bence en önemli farkı, sadece katılımcı seviyesinin üst düzey olması değil. Bugüne kadarki bütün COP'larda aslında taahhütler konuşuluyordu, bu COP'ta uygulama COP'u olarak geçiyor. Yani artık taahhütlerden uygulamaya geçme, artık söylenenlerin arkasında net bir şekilde durma COP'u. O anlamda çok önemli bir COP olduğunu düşünüyorum." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. "Türkiye'nin yaklaşık 50 milyar dolar enerji ithalatı var" Türkiye'nin enerji ithalatçısı bir ülke olduğuna dikkati çeken Tan, sürdürülebilirlik yatırımlarının ülke ekonomisi açısından büyük önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Tan, Türkiye'nin geçen yıl yaklaşık 50 milyar dolar enerji ithalatı gerçekleştirdiğini belirterek, "Bizim gibi enerji ithalatçısı ülkeler için açıkçası sürdürülebilirlik tarafı her şeyden önemli, daha ötede bir önem taşıyor. Çünkü Türkiye'nin ciddi bir enerji ithalatı var. Geçtiğimiz yıl yaklaşık 50 milyar dolar civarında enerji ithalatımız var ve bu, dış ticaret açığımızın önemli bir kısmını oluşturuyor. Bunu daha netleştirmek ve ekonomiye daha pozitif katkısını sağlamak açısından mutlaka içerideki sürdürülebilir yatırımları yapmamız gerekiyor." ifadelerini kullandı. Elektrifikasyonun önümüzdeki yıllarda gündemden düşmemesi gereken konulardan biri olduğunu belirten Tan, dünyadaki enerji tüketiminde elektriğin payının 2035'te yüzde 35'e çıkarılmasının hedeflendiğini aktardı. Tan, bugün söz konusu oranın yüzde 23 seviyesinde bulunduğunu kaydederek, "Eğer bu hedef gerçekleştirilirse hem dünya için hem de tabii ki Türkiye için hem çevresel faktörlerde hem de ekonomiye olan yansımalarıyla çok önemli bir gelişme olacağını düşünüyorum. Bu zirvenin de belki en önemli başarı kriterlerinden bir tanesi, inşallah önümüzdeki hafta sonunda bütün dünya liderleri bu konuda mutabakata varırlarsa, 2035 yılında dünyadaki enerji tüketiminin yüzde 35'inin elektrikten geldiği noktaya ulaşmak olacak. Çok başarılı bir sonuç olacağını düşünüyorum." dedi. "Dış kaynaklarımızın yüzde 35'i sürdürülebilir kaynaklardan" QNB Türkiye'nin sürdürülebilir finansman alanında aktif bir banka olduğunu belirten Tan, bankanın yaklaşık 11 milyar dolar dış kaynağı bulunduğunu bildirdi. Tan, bu kaynağın yüzde 35'inin sürdürülebilir finansman kaynaklarından sağlandığını ve müşterilere sürdürülebilir kredi olarak kullandırıldığını belirterek, şöyle devam etti: "QNB Türkiye olarak bu konuda çok aktif bir bankayız. Bizim öncelikle sürdürülebilir finansmandaki aktifliğimiz sürdürülebilir kaynaklarımızdan geliyor. Bankamızın yaklaşık 11 milyar dolar civarında bir dış kaynağı, yurt dışı fonlamamız var. Bu 11 milyar doların yüzde 35'lik kısmını bugün sürdürülebilir kaynaklardan alıyoruz ve bunu müşterilerimize sürdürülebilir kredi olarak veriyoruz. O da yaklaşık 5,8 milyar dolar seviyesinde, dolar karşılığı TL ile karışık olan bir kredi var. Bu konudaki oranlarımızı her geçen gün artırmak istiyoruz." Bankanın net sıfır hedefinin 2050 yılı olduğunu hatırlatan Tan, "Günün sonunda bizim geçtiğimiz yıllarda verdiğimiz bir taahhüdümüz var. O da QNB Türkiye'nin 2050 yılında net sıfır karbon hedefi. Bu hedefin arkasında durmak açısından hem kendi tüketimimizi hem kredi verdiğimiz müşterilerimizin emisyonlarını aşağı doğru çekerek bu hedefler doğrultusunda devam etmek istiyoruz." ifadelerini kullandı. 500 milyon dolarlık finansman 5 farklı kalkınma bankasından sağlandı COP31 kapsamında imzalanan 500 milyon dolarlık anlaşmanın detaylarını da paylaşan Tan, finansmanın 5 yıl vadeli olduğunu ve dünyadaki 5 önemli kalkınma bankasından sağlandığını belirtti. Anlaşmanın yalnızca emisyon azaltımına yönelik olmadığını, çok sayıda farklı alanı kapsadığını vurgulayan Tan, şunları kaydetti: "Gerçekten çok önemli bir anlaşmaydı. 500 milyon dolar, 5 yıl vadeli sürdürülebilir bir kaynak sağladık. Ama bu anlaşmanın diğer önemli kısmı, 500 milyon doları dünyadaki 5 önemli ayrı kalkınma bankasından ayrı ayrı aldık. Yani 150 milyon dolarla 50 milyon doları 80 kaynaklar aldık. Daha da bence önemlisi, sadece tek bir amaca hitap etmiyor. Sadece tek bir emisyon azalımı veya değişimle ilgili değil, çok kapsamlı bir anlaşma. Bunun içinde hem çevresel faktörler var, yeşil dönüşüm var, elektrifikasyon var. Diğer tarafta kadın istihdamının artışı var veya deprem bölgesi ve yatırım öncelikli bölgelerdeki KOBİ'lerin gelişimi var. Çok geniş kapsamlı bir anlaşma. O anlamda çok önemsiyoruz." Söz konusu anlaşmanın bankanın sürdürülebilir finansman hacmine katkı sağlayacağını belirten Tan, "Bugün COP'ta bunu imzalamak bizim açımızdan ayrı bir gurur oldu. Bu 3,5 milyar dolarlık sürdürülebilir finansmanımızın üzerine 500 milyon dolar daha eklemiş olduk. Önümüzdeki yıllarda bu oranımızı hep artırmak istiyoruz." dedi. Sürdürülebilir yatırımların yalnızca çevresel faktörler açısından değil, Türkiye ekonomisinin gelişimi bakımından da önemli olduğunu ifade eden Tan, enerji bağımlılığının azaltılmasının ekonomik göstergelere olumlu yansıyacağını belirterek, "Dışa bağımlılığımızı, enerji bağımlılığımızı azalttığımız zaman mutlaka büyümeye, dış ticarete ve enflasyona çok pozitif etkisi olacağını düşünüyoruz. Bankaların da burada önemli bir yer tuttuğunu düşünüyoruz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.

news.articleText: Bulls Yatırım'dan KAP açıklaması: 5,4 milyar TL'lik borçlanma planına SPK engeli - Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler'in 5,4 milyar TL nominal değerli borçlanma aracı ihracı için SPK'ye yaptığı başvuru, şirket faaliyetlerinin geçici olarak durdurulması nedeniyle işlemden kaldırıldı. Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler'in 5,4 milyar TL nominal değerli borçlanma aracı ihracı için Sermaye Piyasası Kuruluna (SPK) yaptığı başvuru, şirketin faaliyetlerinin geçici olarak durdurulması nedeniyle işlemden kaldırıldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler, Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformuna (KAP) yaptığı açıklamada, yurt içinde halka arz edilmeksizin nitelikli yatırımcılara ve/veya tahsisli olarak gerçekleştirilmesi planlanan borçlanma aracı ihracına ilişkin başvurunun işlemden kaldırıldığını bildirdi. Şirketin 2 Eylül 2026 tarihli yetkili organ kararı doğrultusunda hazırlanan 5 milyar 400 milyon TL nominal değerli borçlanma aracı ihraç tavanına ilişkin başvuru, 7 Eylül'de SPK'ye yapılmıştı. Açıklamada, SPK tarafından şirkete iletilen yazıda, şirket faaliyetlerinin geçici olarak durdurulduğunun dikkate alındığı ve borçlanma aracı ihraç limiti verilmesi talepli başvurunun işlemden kaldırılmasına karar verildiğinin bildirildiği kaydedildi.

news.titleTr: Euro Bölgesi'nde büyüme yavaşladı
news.summaryTr: Euro Bölgesi ve Avrupa Birliği ekonomilerinin yılın üçüncü çeyreğindeki büyüme performansı belli oldu. Euro Bölgesi ekonomisi üçüncü çeyrekte yüzde 0,4 büyürken Avrupa Birliği yüzde 0,5 büyüdü.
news.articleText: Euro Bölgesi'nde büyüme yavaşladı - Euro Bölgesi ve Avrupa Birliği ekonomilerinin yılın üçüncü çeyreğindeki büyüme performansı belli oldu. Euro Bölgesi ekonomisi üçüncü çeyrekte yüzde 0,4 büyürken Avrupa Birliği yüzde 0,5 büyüdü. Euro Bölgesi ekonomisi, bu yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde önceki çeyreğe kıyasla yüzde 0,4 büyüme kaydetti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Avrupa İstatistik Ofisi (Eurostat), Avrupa Birliği (AB) ile Euro Bölgesi'nin 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyrek dönemine ilişkin Gayri Safi Yurt İçi Hasıla (GSYH) ve istihdam öncü verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre, Euro Bölgesi'nde mevsimsellikten arındırılmış GSYH, yılın üçüncü çeyreğinde ikinci çeyreğe kıyasla yüzde 0,4 arttı. GSYH, üçüncü çeyrekte geçen yılın aynı dönemine kıyasla da yüzde 1,3 yükseldi. AB'de ise mevsimsellikten arındırılmış GSYH, üçüncü çeyrekte çeyreklik bazda yüzde 0,5, yıllık bazda yüzde 1,5 arttı. Yılın ikinci çeyreğinde Euro Bölgesi ekonomisi çeyreklik bazda yüzde 0,6, AB ekonomisi ise yüzde 0,7 büyümüştü. GSYH, üçüncü çeyrekte önceki çeyreğe kıyasla Almanya'da yüzde 0,2 ve İspanya'da yüzde 0,6 artarken, Fransa'da yüzde 0,1 geriledi. İtalya ekonomisi ise aynı dönemde değişim göstermedi. Yıllık bazda GSYH, İspanya'da yüzde 2,7, Almanya'da yüzde 1,2 ve İtalya'da yüzde 0,8 yükselirken, Fransa'da yüzde 0,1 düştü. Üçüncü çeyrekte istihdam hem Euro Bölgesi'nde hem de AB'de önceki çeyreğe kıyasla sabit kaldı. İstihdam, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre ise her iki bölgede de yüzde 0,4 artış gösterdi.

news.title: AB'nin dış ticaret dengesi negatife döndü: Eylülde 16,8 milyar euro açık
news.summary: Eurostat verilerine göre AB, eylülde geçen yılın aynı ayında verdiği 11,4 milyar avroluk dış ticaret fazlasına karşılık bu yıl 16,8 milyar avro açık verdi. Açıkta enerji ticaretindeki bozulma ve makine, taşıt ile kimyasal ürünlerdeki fazlanın azalması etkili oldu.

news.titleTr: AB'nin dış ticaret dengesi negatife döndü: Eylülde 16,8 milyar euro açık
news.summaryTr: Eurostat verilerine göre AB, eylülde geçen yılın aynı ayında verdiği 11,4 milyar avroluk dış ticaret fazlasına karşılık bu yıl 16,8 milyar avro açık verdi. Açıkta enerji ticaretindeki bozulma ve makine, taşıt ile kimyasal ürünlerdeki fazlanın azalması etkili oldu.
news.articleText: AB'nin dış ticaret dengesi negatife döndü: Eylülde 16,8 milyar euro açık - Eurostat verilerine göre AB, eylülde geçen yılın aynı ayında verdiği 11,4 milyar avroluk dış ticaret fazlasına karşılık bu yıl 16,8 milyar avro açık verdi. Açıkta enerji ticaretindeki bozulma ve makine, taşıt ile kimyasal ürünlerdeki fazlanın azalması etkili oldu. Avrupa Birliği (AB), eylül ayında enerji ticaretindeki açığın artması ve makine ile taşıt ticaretindeki fazlanın azalmasıyla 16,8 milyar avro dış ticaret açığı verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Avrupa İstatistik Ofisi (Eurostat), Euro Bölgesi ve AB'nin eylül ayı uluslararası ticaret verilerini açıkladı. Buna göre, Euro Bölgesi'nin ihracatı, eylülde geçen yılın aynı dönemine kıyasla yüzde 6 artarak 272,7 milyar euroya, ithalatı ise yüzde 16,1 yükselerek 283 milyar euroya ulaştı. Böylece Euro Bölgesi, eylülde 10,3 milyar avro dış ticaret açığı verdi. Avro Bölgesi, geçen yılın eylül ayında 13,5 milyar euro dış ticaret fazlası, bu yıl ağustosta ise 16,6 milyar avro dış ticaret açığı vermişti. AB'nin ihracatı ise eylülde geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 4,7 artarak 240,1 milyar euroya, ithalatı da yüzde 17,9 yükselerek 256,9 milyar euroya çıktı. Böylece AB, eylülde 16,8 milyar avro dış ticaret açığı verdi. AB, geçen yılın aynı ayında 11,4 milyar avro dış ticaret fazlası, bu yıl ağustosta ise 25,3 milyar avro dış ticaret açığı vermişti. Avrupa'nın dış ticaretinde enerji faturası ağırlaştı AB'nin ticaretindeki değişim enerji ürünlerindeki açığın artmasından, makine, araç ve kimyasal ürünlerdeki fazlanın ise gerilemesinden kaynaklandı. Eylülde AB'den en fazla ithalat yapan ülkeler, 47,7 milyar euroyla ABD, 33,5 milyar euroyla İngiltere, 21,5 milyar euroyla İsviçre, 16,5 milyar euroyla Çin ve 9,7 milyar euroyla Türkiye oldu. Aynı dönemde AB'ye en fazla ihracat yapan ülkeler ise 58,2 milyar euroyla Çin, 36,8 milyar euroyla ABD, 14,8 milyar avroyla İngiltere, 12,6 milyar avroyla Norveç, 12,5 milyar euroyla İsviçre ve 8,5 milyar avroyla Türkiye olarak sıralandı. Ocak-eylül döneminde Euro Bölgesi'nin dış ticaret açığı 36,5 milyar euro, AB'nin dış ticaret açığı ise 83,2 milyar euro oldu.
