news.articleText: Emekli zammında seyyanen artış ve refah payı: İşte Ocak 2027 maaş senaryoları Ocak 2027 emekli zammı için refah payı ve seyyanen artış formülleri gündemde. Dr. Okan Güray Bülbül, emekli maaşlarına ilişkin çalışmaların sürdüğünü belirtirken, en düşük emekli aylığının 33 bin TL'ye yükseltilmesi halinde kök maaşa göre olası zam senaryolarını anlattı. Milyonlarca emeklinin gözü Ocak 2027'de yapılacak maaş artışına çevrildi. Enflasyon farkının yanı sıra refah payı ve seyyanen zam formülleri de gündemde yer alırken, en düşük emekli aylığının ne kadar olacağı merak ediliyor. Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli Üniversitesi Öğretim Üyesi Dr. Okan Güray Bülbül, emeklilere yönelik yürütülen çalışmaları ve olası zam senaryolarını değerlendirdi. Bülbül, emeklilere refah payı verilmesine ilişkin henüz netleşen bir karar olmadığını belirterek, Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK) ve Maliye Bakanlığı'nın bu konuda çalışmalar yürüttüğünü söyledi. Emeklilerin beklentisinin giderek arttığına dikkat çeken Bülbül, "Emeklilere refah payı ile ilgili şu anda netleşen bir şey yok, çalışmalar devam ediyor. Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu ve Maliye Bakanlığı'nın bu konuda çalışma yaptığını biliyoruz. Ama beklentinin günbegün daha da arttığını söyleyebiliriz" dedi. Emekli maaşları için hangi formüller gündemde? Bülbül, Ocak 2027'de emekli aylıklarına yapılabilecek artışlara ilişkin farklı senaryoları da anlattı. Yüzde 12'lik enflasyon zammının yanı sıra yüzde 8 ve yüzde 13'lük refah payı ile 5 bin TL ve 10 bin TL'lik seyyanen artış seçenekleri üzerinden hesaplamalar yapıldı. En düşük emekli aylığının 23 bin 552 TL'den 33 bin TL'ye yükseltilmesi ihtimalinin de ele alındığı hesaplamalarda, kök aylıklara göre farklı maaş tutarları ortaya çıktı. Kök maaşa göre emekli zammı hesaplamaları 18 bin TL kök aylığı olan emekli: Kasım ayında 23 bin 552 TL alan emeklinin kök aylığı yüzde 12 enflasyon zammıyla 20 bin 160 TL'ye yükseliyor. Yüzde 8 refah payı senaryosunda 21 bin 600 TL, 5 bin TL seyyanen zam senaryosunda 25 bin 160 TL, yüzde 13 refah payı senaryosunda 22 bin 500 TL ve 10 bin TL seyyanen zam senaryosunda 30 bin 160 TL hesaplanıyor. En düşük emekli aylığının 33 bin TL'ye çıkarılması halinde ödenecek aylık 33 bin TL oluyor. 20 bin TL kök aylığı olan emekli: Kasım ayında 23 bin 552 TL alan emeklinin aylığı yüzde 12 enflasyon zammıyla 22 bin 400 TL'ye çıkıyor. Yüzde 8 refah payı senaryosunda 24 bin TL, 5 bin TL seyyanen artışla 27 bin 400 TL, yüzde 13 refah payı senaryosunda 25 bin TL ve 10 bin TL seyyanen artışla 32 bin 400 TL hesaplanıyor. En düşük aylığın 33 bin TL olması halinde emekliye 33 bin TL ödeniyor. 22 bin TL kök aylığı olan emekli: Mevcut durumda 23 bin 552 TL alan emeklinin kök aylığı yüzde 12 enflasyon zammıyla 24 bin 640 TL'ye yükseliyor. Yüzde 8 refah payı senaryosunda 26 bin 400 TL, 5 bin TL seyyanen zamla 29 bin 640 TL, yüzde 13 refah payı senaryosunda 27 bin 500 TL ve 10 bin TL seyyanen zamla 34 bin 640 TL'ye ulaşıyor. Son senaryoda Ocak 2027'de ödenecek aylık 34 bin 640 TL oluyor. 24 bin TL kök aylığı olan emekli: Kasım ayında 24 bin TL alan emeklinin aylığı yüzde 12 enflasyon zammıyla 26 bin 880 TL'ye çıkıyor. Yüzde 8 refah payı senaryosunda 28 bin 800 TL, 5 bin TL seyyanen artışla 31 bin 880 TL, yüzde 13 refah payı senaryosunda 30 bin TL ve 10 bin TL seyyanen artışla 36 bin 880 TL hesaplanıyor. Son senaryoda ödenecek aylık 36 bin 880 TL oluyor. 26 bin TL kök aylığı olan emekli: Yüzde 12 enflasyon zammıyla emeklinin aylığı 29 bin 120 TL'ye yükseliyor. news.summary: Microsoft'un Outlook, Teams ve Copilot hizmetlerinde 12 saati aşan kesintinin ardından normalleşme süreci başladı. Dünya genelinde şirketlerden kamu kurumlarına kadar geniş bir kullanıcı kitlesini etkileyen aksaklık, finansal işlemlerden kurumsal iletişime kadar pek çok alanda tıkanıklık yaratmıştı.

news.titleTr: Microsoft'tan kesinti açıklaması: Trafik kademeli olarak normale dönüyor
news.summaryTr: Microsoft'un Outlook, Teams ve Copilot hizmetlerinde 12 saati aşan kesintinin ardından normalleşme süreci başladı. Dünya genelinde şirketlerden kamu kurumlarına kadar geniş bir kullanıcı kitlesini etkileyen aksaklık, finansal işlemlerden kurumsal iletişime kadar pek çok alanda tıkanıklık yaratmıştı.
news.articleText: Microsoft'tan kesinti açıklaması: Trafik kademeli olarak normale dönüyor - Microsoft'un Outlook, Teams ve Copilot hizmetlerinde 12 saati aşan kesintinin ardından normalleşme süreci başladı. - Dünya genelinde şirketlerden kamu kurumlarına kadar geniş bir kullanıcı kitlesini etkileyen aksaklık, finansal işlemlerden kurumsal iletişime kadar pek çok alanda farklı sorunları beraberinde getirdi. Microsoft, Outlook, Teams ve Copilot başta olmak üzere hizmetlerinde yaşanan kesintinin ardından trafiğin kademeli olarak normale döndüğünü bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, kritik kullanım alanlarında iyileşmeler görüldüğünü ve etkilenen altyapının bazı bölümlerinde kurtarma çalışmalarının tamamlandığını açıkladı. Microsoft, hizmet kesintisine ilişkin son güncellemesinde yeniden sağlanan hizmetlerde ek ilerleme kaydedildiğini belirtti. Şirket, trafiğin kademeli olarak normale döndüğünü ve müşterilerin kritik kullanım alanlarında iyileşmeler görüldüğünü duyurdu. Etkilenen altyapının bazı bölümlerinde kurtarma çalışmalarının tamamlandığı, hizmetlerin kalıcı olarak yeniden sağlanması için daha geniş kapsamlı düzeltmelerin uygulandığı bildirildi. Outlook, Teams ve Copilot uygulamalarındaki kesinti 12 saati aşarken, dünya genelindeki şirketlerin ve kamu kurumlarının iletişiminde aksamalara neden oldu. Microsoft, kesintinin kaynağını sunucu sorunlarına bağladı ve herhangi bir kötü niyetli faaliyetten haberdar olmadığını açıkladı. Aksaklıktan Avustralya, Japonya ve ABD'deki kamu kurumları etkilendi. Kesinti, ticaret şirketlerinde işlemlerin aksamasına, şirketlerin finansal sonuçlarını açıklamasında gecikmelere ve havayollarının yolcularını iletişim hizmetlerindeki sorunlar konusunda uyarmasına yol açtı. Finansal işlemlerde faks dönemi Avrupa'da borsa işletmecisi Euronext, listeleme ekiplerinin e-posta iletişiminde sorunlar yaşadığını bildirdi. İngiliz sigorta şirketi Aviva, finansal sonuç açıklamaları için yedek planlar oluştururken Danimarkalı nakliye şirketi Maersk, müşterilerini e-posta ve güncellemelerde yaşanan gecikmeler konusunda uyardı. ABD merkezli yapay zeka şirketleri OpenAI ve Anthropic, Microsoft bağlantılarıyla ilgili sorunlar yaşadıklarını açıkladı. Hindistan merkezli havayolları IndiGo, Akasa Air ve Air India da e-posta destek hizmetlerinin kesintiden etkilendiğini bildirdi. Kesinti, Tayvan'daki menkul kıymet şirketleri, hayat sigortacıları ve yatırım fonu şirketlerinin fon yönetimi faaliyetlerini de aksattı. Konuya yakın bir kaynağın Reuters'e verdiği bilgiye göre, şirketlerden biri tahvil geri alım işlemini iptal etti. İkinci bir kaynak ise Tayvan'daki başka bir finans şirketinin işlemleri onaylamak için faks kullanmaya başladığını aktardı. ABD merkezli elektrikli kamyon üreticisi Workhorse Group, perşembe günü açıklamayı planladığı finansal sonuçlarını 16 Kasım'a erteledi. İsviçreli Richemont ise cuma günü ilk yarıyıl sonuçlarının açıklanmasını kısa süreliğine geciktirdi. Microsoft 365'te bu yıl ikinci kesinti Microsoft 365 hizmetlerinde bu yıl ocak ayında ve geçen yıl ekim ayında da kesintiler yaşandı. Şirket, geçen ay ise üretkenlik yazılım paketini ve dünya genelindeki çeşitli sektörleri etkileyen Azure bulut platformunda bir kesinti bildirdi. eToro işlem platformunda piyasa analisti olarak görev yapan Josh Gilbert, az sayıda müşterinin Microsoft ekosisteminden kısa sürede ayrılabilmesi nedeniyle yatırımcıların mevcut kesintiyi şimdilik tolere edeceğini söyledi. Gilbert, bu yıl Microsoft 365 hizmetlerinde yaşanan kesintilerin tekrarlanmasının güvenilirlik konusunda soru işaretleri oluşturabileceğini belirterek, BT departmanlarının iş süreçlerinin daha büyük bölümünü tek bir sağlayıcıya emanet etmeden önce yeniden değerlendirme yapabileceğini ifade etti. Kamu kurumları da kesintiden etkilendi Avustralya Siber Güvenlik Bakanı Tony Burke, Microsoft'un bir siber saldırıyla karşı karşıya olmadığına inandığını söyledi. Burke, kesintinin etkisinin büyük ölçüde e-posta sistemlerinde yoğunlaştığını belirtti. Avustralya'nın istihbarat teşkilatı ve federal polisi de cuma günü yaşanan kesintiden etkilenen kurumlar arasında yer aldı. ABD Temsilciler Meclisi, kullanıcılarının kesintiden etkilendiğini ve mühendislerinin Microsoft ile birlikte çalıştığını açıkladı. Japonya Başbakan Yardımcısı Masanao Ozaki de kesintinin hükümetin bilgi sistemi altyapısını etkilediğini bildirdi. Microsoft'un hizmet sağlığı bildiriminde, Exchange Online ile e-posta hizmetlerine bağlı Microsoft 365 özelliklerinin kesintiden etkilendiği belirtildi. Exchange Online'a bağlı olmayan hizmet bileşenlerinin ise çalışmayı sürdürdüğü kaydedildi. Exchange Online, Microsoft'un e-posta, takvim, kişiler ve görev hizmetleri sunan bulut tabanlı mesajlaşma platformu olarak faaliyet gösteriyor.

news.articleText: TV reyting ölçümlerine Rekabet Kurumu el attı: Soruşturma başlatıldı - Rekabet Kurumu, televizyon izleyici ölçümü hizmeti sunan FIFTY5BLUE hakkında resen soruşturma başlattı. İncelemede izleyici panelinin oluşturulması, verilerin işlenmesi ve reyting sonuçlarının raporlanma yöntemleri ele alınacak. Rekabet Kurumu, reyting ölçümleri hakkında soruşturma başlatıldığını açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kurumdan yapılan açıklama şu şekilde: elevizyonda hangi programın yayında kalacağından, milyarlarca liralık reklam bütçesinin hangi kanala gideceğine kadar tüm dengeyi belirleyen reyting ölçümleri hakkında soruşturma başlatıldı. Rekabet Kurumu, reklamcılık sektörüne yönelik yürüttüğü incelemede elde ettiği bulgular doğrultusunda, televizyon izleyici ölçümü hizmeti sunan FIFTY5BLUE hakkında resen soruşturma açılmasına karar verdi. Reyting verileri neden bu kadar kritik? Reyting sonuçları yalnızca bir kanalın veya programın ne kadar izlendiğini değil, hangi izleyici gruplarına ulaşıldığını da gösteriyor. Reklamverenler ve medya planlama ajansları, hedef kitleye ulaşma maliyetini bu verilere göre hesaplayıp bütçelerini yönlendiriyor. Televizyon kanalları, izleyici erişimlerini bu sonuçlarla ortaya koyarak reklam fiyatlarını belirliyor ve reklam pastasından pay almak için rekabet ediyor. Bu nedenle ölçüm verilerinin güvenilir ve karşılaştırılabilir olması, tüm sektördeki adil rekabetin anahtarını oluşturuyor. Soruşturmada neler incelenecek? Rekabet Kurumu; ölçüm uygulamalarının sonuçlarını ve bu ölçümlerin televizyon reklamcılığındaki rekabet koşullarını nasıl etkilediğini mercek altına alacak. Bu kapsamda FIFTY5BLUE'nun; ölçüme esas verileri nasıl kullandığı, izleyici panelindeki haneleri nasıl oluşturup yönettiği, izleme kayıtlarını ne şekilde işlediği, ölçüm sonuçlarını hangi yöntemle raporladığı ve tüm bu süreçlerde Rekabeti ihlal edip etmediği incelenecek.

news.title: Ariel Investments CEO'sundan yapay zeka uyarısı: 1999 balonu yeniden yaşanabilir
news.summary: Ariel Investments CEO'su Mellody Hobson, yapay zeka yatırımlarındaki hızlı büyümeyi 1999'daki dot-com balonuna benzeterek milyarlarca dolarlık harcamaların nasıl kâra dönüşeceğinin belirsiz olduğunu söyledi.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ariel Investments CEO'sundan yapay zeka uyarısı: 1999 balonu yeniden yaşanabilir
news.summaryTr: Ariel Investments CEO'su Mellody Hobson, yapay zeka yatırımlarındaki hızlı büyümeyi 1999'daki dot-com balonuna benzeterek milyarlarca dolarlık harcamaların nasıl kâra dönüşeceğinin belirsiz olduğunu söyledi.
news.articleText: Ariel Investments CEO'sundan yapay zeka uyarısı: 1999 balonu yeniden yaşanabilir - Ariel Investments CEO'su Mellody Hobson, yapay zeka yatırımlarındaki hızlı büyümeyi 1999'daki dot-com balonuna benzeterek milyarlarca dolarlık harcamaların nasıl kâra dönüşeceğinin belirsiz olduğunu söyledi. - Hobson, piyasaların Anthropic'in olası halka arzına aşırı anlam yüklemesini de riskli buldu. Ariel Investments Eş Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Mellody Hobson, küresel piyasaların Anthropic'in olası halka arzına aşırı anlam yüklemesini endişe verici bulduğunu belirtti. Yapay zeka yatırımlarındaki hızlı büyümeyi 1999'daki dot-com balonuna benzeten Hobson, şirketlerin milyarlarca dolarlık harcamalarının kâra nasıl dönüşeceğinin henüz net olmadığını söyledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Yahoo Finance'ın haberine göre Hobson, ekim ayı sonunda yaptığı değerlendirmede, piyasanın tamamının tek bir halka arzın performansına bağlanmasına dikkati çekti. Anthropic'in halka arzı endişe yarattı Hobson, “Piyasanın tamamının tek bir halka arzın, özellikle de Anthropic'in, gidişatına bağlı olacağını söyleyen haberler okumaya başlamak endişe verici” dedi. Binlerce farklı sektörden şirketin işlem gördüğü bir piyasada bu ölçüde tek bir yatırıma odaklanılmasının riskli olduğunu belirten Hobson, Ariel Investments'ın kısa vadeli alım satım yerine uzun vadeli yatırım yaklaşımını benimsediğini vurguladı. Yapay zeka yatırımlarında dot-com benzetmesi Hobson, mevcut piyasa ortamını 1999'daki teknoloji balonuna benzeterek, yatırımcıların aynı şirket ve sektörlere yönelmesinin değerlemeleri şişirdiğini ifade etti. Yapay zeka alanında yüksek tutarlı yatırımlar yapıldığını ancak bu harcamaların nasıl bir kârlılık sağlayacağının henüz netleşmediğini belirten Hobson, piyasanın zaman zaman yatırımların karşılığını vereceğine inandığını, zaman zaman ise harcanan milyarlarca doların nasıl kâra dönüşeceğini sorguladığını söyledi. Hobson ayrıca yapay zeka şirketleri arasındaki karşılıklı finansman ilişkilerine de dikkati çekerek, şirketlerin birbirlerine yatırım yaptığı bu döngüsel finansman yapısının endişe verici olduğunu dile getirdi. Piyasalarda oynaklık arttı Son haftalarda ABD ara seçimleri, büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin finansal sonuçları ve yüksek sermaye harcamaları piyasalardaki dalgalanmayı artırdı. Nvidia CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın görevinden ayrılması da teknoloji ve yapay zeka bağlantılı hisselerde satış baskısını güçlendirdi. Orta Doğu'daki jeopolitik gerilimlerin etkisiyle petrol fiyatlarının yüksek seyretmesi, enflasyonun kalıcı olabileceği endişelerini yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Bu gelişmeler, uzun vadeli ABD Hazine tahvili faizlerinin de yüksek seviyelerde kalmasına yol açtı. Ariel Investments'ın kurucu ortağı John Rogers ile birlikte şirketi yöneten Hobson, daha önce Starbucks'ın yönetim kurulu başkanlığını yaptı. JPMorgan Chase yönetim kurulunda görevini sürdüren Hobson, NFL takımlarından Denver Broncos'un da azınlık hissedarları arasında bulunuyor.

news.title: Unocoin keeps deposits and withdrawals halted over suspect transfers
news.summary: Unocoin said the transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform, and BitGo said the account freeze worked as intended.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Unocoin keeps deposits and withdrawals halted over suspect transfers
news.summaryTr: Unocoin said the transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform, and BitGo said the account freeze worked as intended.
news.articleText: Unocoin keeps deposits and withdrawals halted over suspect transfers Unocoin said the transfers were signed outside BitGo’s platform while its account was frozen, possibly via a wallet recovery feature. Indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin has kept deposits and withdrawals suspended as it investigates whether suspicious transfers from wallets linked to custodian BitGo were made using a recovery feature. On Friday, the exchange said that BitGo had frozen the exchange’s enterprise account on Nov. 6 at Unocoin’s request and that the freeze worked as intended. The transactions under investigation were signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform, Unocoin said. The exchange said BitGo’s multisignature wallets include a recovery feature that lets wallet holders access funds if BitGo becomes unavailable. Unocoin suspects the feature was misused and has yet to establish how the transfers occured or whether it lost any digital assets. Unocoin and BiGo did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for more information before publication. Unocoin first the unauthorized activity on Nov. 6 and suspended all services on Monday after detecting further activity. On Thursday, it disclosed outgoing transactions from an Ethereum address in its BitGo wallet infrastructure and said its servers had been compromised. The exchange has not announced a date for restoring services. A Nov. 5 warning from India’s cybersecurity agency described an AI-assisted campaign targeting crypto exchanges and other financial firms. No connection to Unocoin’s incident has been established. news.title: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?
news.summary: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?
news.summaryTr: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
news.articleText: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need? - Published Floorplans. Air duct diagrams. Heat pump specifications. Most people in the market for a new heating system probably don't want to think about this level of detail. But, perhaps surprisingly, some do want to think about those things. In extreme depth. Every day, roughly 150 new users sign up to an app called Cool Calc, which works out the heat requirements of properties in the US. Just over one third of those new users are not tradespeople but private homeowners, says founder and chief executive Bill Fiore. When choosing a heating system, people can find themselves bombarded with information – how powerful a heat pump do they need, for example? It isn't always easy to take a tradesperson at their word. "As an overall trend, we are seeing homeowners be more informed," explains Fiore. "They want to do a calculation on their own." A heat loss calculation is a figure, usually measured in watts, that defines how much heat a home loses during cold weather. It's worked out room by room and is a key part of designing an efficient heating system. This estimate is especially important to get right when installing a heat pump, which is sized fairly precisely, according to the projected heat loss. Should that calculation be off, the heat pump will likely perform poorly. You could be left with an underpowered device that struggles to warm your property, for example. Given the costs involved, homeowners are often anxious to ensure installers avoid such mistakes. Certain new technologies are not, for the moment, helping, adds Fiore. "People are going to AI and they're getting a lot of misinformation because it's not backed by anything credible," he says. Cool Calc is planning to integrate with AI chatbots to try and improve the quality of the advice they spew out. It is probably a good idea to be cautious about your new heating system's design, says Kevin Kircher at Purdue University. He and colleagues recently conducted a study, yet to be published, examining the heat loss calculations provided by tradespeople to roughly 75 US homeowners. "We were surprised," says Kircher. "The heat loss calculations often led to overestimating the design heat loads by a factor of two or more." That would result in oversized systems that use much more power than necessary. Not only that, some people reported charges of more than $1,000 (£745) – and in one case as much as $2,500 – just for a heat loss survey, adds Kircher. Besides using excessive amounts of energy, an oversized heating system can also feel uncomfortable, says Dan Dempsey, a former senior engineering fellow for a major heating and cooling provider in the US. Dempsey, who took part in Kircher and his colleagues' study, lives in Indiana. He says it is his retirement hobby to monitor the performance of heating and cooling systems in the homes of friends and family members, by analysing data from their smart thermostats. "I spent five years manually downloading everything, every week," he says. He points out that oversized systems tend to cycle a lot, meaning they switch on and off again in quick succession. This leads to discernible swings in temperature: rooms that fail to remain at their target temperature of, say, 20C, but rather fluctuate, which feels uncomfortable, says Dempsey. For people seeking a better understanding of their home's heat loss, various free or partially free apps, including Cool Calc and AutoHVAC, are available. There are options for UK homeowners, too, such as web app Heatpunk. Many things can influence the heat loss figure, including the amount of insulation in your home, whether the building has double or triple glazing, and also the size of your radiators. Heatpunk allows people to draw a floor plan of their home and input data about the property in order to estimate its performance. Thousands of people use it every month, mostly professional installers, says Andy Rankin, founder and managing director of Midsummer Energy. The web app also suggests specific heat pump models for each property, based on the results of the calculation. Naturally, these are models available through Midsummer Energy. "It's been a very effective marketing tool," says Rankin. Dwellow, another company that offers heat pump installations in the UK, is keen to follow suit. The firm recently launched its own heat loss estimator. While professional heat loss calculations remain essential, getting people to do their own "self surveys" first could ultimately reduce how much time professional heating engineers must spend analysing properties says Ian Mclaren, Dwellow's co-founder and director. "Going into a home and just being able to check the information rather than start from scratch could turn a survey into a half-hour trip – far more efficient and less costly," says Mclaren. There's no substitute for engineers doing a good job when it is their turn, however, stresses Maurizio Sibilla, of the Centre for Advanced Built Environment Research at the University of West England, Bristol. "The solution is better installer practice, clearer customer-facing evidence, and improved methods, not expecting homeowners to do the engineering themselves," he says, adding that providing homeowners with information about the calculation and also data on heat pump performance post-installation can reassure them that the system works as expected. Doing your own heat loss calculation may end up "over-intellectualising" things, says Adam Chapman, chief geek at heat pump training firm and installer network Heat Geek. "I don't personally see what a homeowner would gain from it," he says. "We will guarantee the efficiency with way less radiators and pipework upgrades than any other system out there." Chapman points out that only the most careful of surveys will capture a home's heat loss well. He says it is common for Heat Geek installers to discover retrofitted windows that haven't been foam-insulated into their openings, leaving draughty gaps, or cavity walls that a homeowner thought had been insulated – but which were actually missed by the builder. "It's stuff you can't see," he says. "What we actually need is home surveys that go and spot for these sorts of things." He and colleagues recently conducted a study, yet to be published, examining the heat loss calculations provided by tradespeople to roughly 75 US homeowners. "We were surprised," says Kircher. "The heat loss calculations often led to overestimating the design heat loads by a factor of two or more." That would result in oversized systems that use much more power than necessary. Not only that, some people reported charges of more than $1,000 (£745) – and in one case as much as $2,500 – just for a heat loss survey, adds Kircher. Besides using excessive amounts of energy, an oversized heating system can also feel uncomfortable, says Dan Dempsey, a former senior engineering fellow for a major heating and cooling provider in the US. Dempsey, who took part in Kircher and his colleagues' study, lives in Indiana. He says it is his retirement hobby to monitor the performance of heating and cooling systems in the homes of friends and family members, by analysing data from their smart thermostats. "I spent five years manually downloading everything, every week," he says. He points out that oversized systems tend to cycle a lot, meaning they switch on and off again in quick succession. This leads to discernible swings in temperature: rooms that fail to remain at their target temperature of, say, 20C, but rather fluctuate, which feels uncomfortable, says Dempsey. For people seeking a better understanding of their home's heat loss, various free or partially free apps, including Cool Calc and AutoHVAC, are available. There are options for UK homeowners, too, such as web app Heatpunk. Many things can influence the heat loss figure, including the amount of insulation in your home, whether the building has double or triple glazing, and also the size of your radiators. Heatpunk allows people to draw a floor plan of their home and input data about the property in order to estimate its performance. Thousands of people use it every month, mostly professional installers, says Andy Rankin, founder and managing director of Midsummer Energy. The web app also suggests specific heat pump models for each property, based on the results of the calculation. Naturally, these are models available through Midsummer Energy. "It's been a very effective marketing tool," says Rankin. Dwellow, another company that offers heat pump installations in the UK, is keen to follow suit. The firm recently launched its own heat loss estimator. While professional heat loss calculations remain essential, getting people to do their own "self surveys" first could ultimately reduce how much time professional heating engineers must spend analysing properties says Ian Mclaren, Dwellow's co-founder and director. "Going into a home and just being able to check the information rather than start from scratch could turn a survey into a half-hour trip – far more efficient and less costly," says Mclaren. There's no substitute for engineers doing a good job when it is their turn, however, stresses Maurizio Sibilla, of the Centre for Advanced Built Environment Research at the University of West England, Bristol. "The solution is better installer practice, clearer customer-facing evidence, and improved methods, not expecting homeowners to do the engineering themselves," he says, adding that providing homeowners with information about the calculation and also data on heat pump performance post-installation can reassure them that the system works as expected. Doing your own heat loss calculation may end up "over-intellectualising" things, says Adam Chapman, chief geek at heat pump training firm and installer network Heat Geek. "I don't personally see what a homeowner would gain from it," he says. "We will guarantee the efficiency with way less radiators and pipework upgrades than any other system out there." Chapman points out that only the most careful of surveys will capture a home's heat loss well. He says it is common for Heat Geek installers to discover retrofitted windows that haven't been foam-insulated into their openings, leaving draughty gaps, or cavity walls that a homeowner thought had been insulated – but which were actually missed by the builder. "It's stuff you can't see," he says. "What we actually need is home surveys that go and spot for these sorts of things." news.titleTr: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam
news.summaryTr: Authorities froze over $2.7 billion in Binance hack proceeds, while the separate FaceStealer scam stole over $400 million in 18 months.
news.articleText: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam Authorities froze over $2.7 billion in Binance hack proceeds, while the separate FaceStealer scam stole over $400 million in 18 months. The US Department of Justice said Thursday it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance. The authorization covers part of the more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets that US authorities and private-sector partners have frozen since the Oct. 29 hack. Investigators are still working to recover additional funds, the department said in its announcement. The FBI attributed the Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group in a cyber alert. Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied North Korea’s involvement. Binance said it had covered the affected assets with its own funds and that a new proof-of-reserves snapshot showed at least one-to-one backing for customer assets, according to its Thursday post on X. In November 2025, the DOJ announced a separate enforcement action targeting about $15 million in cryptocurrency linked to North Korean hackers known as APT38. Related: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente FBI warns of FaceStealer’s deepfake video calls In a separate case, US authorities seized cloud infrastructure used in FaceStealer, a North Korean social engineering campaign that stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months, the DOJ said. The hackers used secretly recorded footage of previous victims and AI-generated deepfakes of prominent crypto figures to gain targets’ trust on video calls. They used bogus technical fixes to trick targets into installing malware, the DOJ said. The campaign targeted people working in crypto and Web3. The hackers also increasingly targeted open-source software developers and maintainers in attempts to gain access to their devices and software repository accounts. The FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims under a federal warrant. The bureau also published guidance on how to protect against the scheme and what to do after a compromise in a public advisory. Redacted stills from webcam videos recorded by FaceStealer hackers. Source: FBI The DOJ said the hackers behind FaceStealer are known publicly by several names, including Sapphire Sleet, UNC1069, Dangerous Password, CryptoCore, APT38, BlueNoroff and Stardust Chollima. news.title: Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT
news.summary: Jane Street ended Q3 with 19% fewer shares in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF, and a higher share price lifted the stake’s value to $957 million.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT
news.summaryTr: Jane Street ended Q3 with 19% fewer shares in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF, and a higher share price lifted the stake’s value to $957 million.
news.articleText: Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT Jane Street ended Q3 with 19% fewer shares in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF, and a higher share price lifted the stake’s value to $957 million. Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%. The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings. Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million. Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday. The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million). JPMorgan adds IBIT shares as Laurore cuts stake JPMorgan Chase increased its IBIT holdings by 9.6% in the third quarter, adding about 1 million shares to reach 11.41 million. The US banking giant’s reported IBIT position rose to around $540 million. In contrast, JPMorgan nearly erased its direct holdings in BlackRock’s ETHA, reducing its position from 1.17 million shares at the end of June to just 399 shares. Related: Barclays boosts BlackRock’s IBIT stake 48% ahead of key Q3 13F filings The bank also increased its holdings in Bitcoin treasury company Strategy by 36% to nearly 849,000 shares, worth about $131 million at the end of Q3. Laurore, which lists a Hong Kong business address in its SEC filing, reduced its IBIT holdings by 33%, cutting its position by 1.6 million shares to 3.25 million, worth about $154 million by the end of Q3. Laurore drew attention in February 2026 after disclosing an IBIT position worth $436 million at the end of 2025. Magazine: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss

news.title: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide
news.summary: Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.

news.titleTr: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide
news.summaryTr: Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.
news.articleText: Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude. A global Microsoft 365 outage continued into Friday, disrupting Outlook email and some Teams features. Microsoft said in a 7:25 am UTC update that a patch had improved stability on some servers and that it was working to deploy the fix more widely. The update, republished by the University of Pennsylvania, gave no timetable for restoration. The outage began Thursday, leaving some users unable to access their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft said a process that handles secure connection became overloaded, causing affected servers to stop processing requests. The company said it attempted to restore services by restarting infrastructure, redirecting network traffic and expanding server capacity. Microsoft said there was no indication of a security breach. The outage also affected features in Microsoft Copilot and Defender for Office 365. In Teams, users had trouble scheduling meetings and sending invitations. Microsoft said most Teams calls and chats continued to work. Businesses and government agencies worldwide use Microsoft 365 for email and scheduling. Microsoft reported more than 450 million paid commercial seats for the suite in an October filing. Exchange Online hosts the mailboxes and calendars those organizations use, and outside apps, including AI assistants, rely on the same service to retrieve that data when users connect their work accounts. OpenAI reported errors in ChatGPT’s Microsoft 365 connector. Anthropic said the outage caused most email, calendar and search requests through Claude’s Microsoft 365 connector to fail. The US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit said its clerk’s office could neither send nor receive email for much of Thursday. Japan’s Finance Ministry said it was unable to receive email on Friday and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency told CNA that government email was among systems affected. news.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
news.summary: Claims the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 sandpaper cheating plot are dividing the cricket world.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
news.summaryTr: Claims the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 sandpaper cheating plot are dividing the cricket world.
news.articleText: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' - Published As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. And there's a sense of injustice that Australia can't seem to escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. In it, he said he had wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the tampering after batsman Cameron Bancroft was caught with the sandpaper on field. "I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'." However Khawaja has since said he didn't want to start a "witch hunt" and has refused to answer questions on exactly who he claims knew of the scheme, and what they knew. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja had written the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve Smith, the captain at the time who was also suspended, has been travelling overseas and is yet to say anything publicly about the claims in the book. Bancroft is also staying silent for now despite previously suggesting the bowlers knew. But half of Australia's living cricket royalty and a slew of former coaches - some of whom have been accused of wrongdoing too - have thrown in their two cents. And Cricket Australia is under pressure from some to reopen its investigation into sandpapergate - something chief executive Todd Greenberg has already ruled out. Prof David Rowe of the University of Western Sydney told the BBC the saga was still so painful for many players and fans as the country sees itself as "a nation of good sports". "The idea of being a good sport is two things. One is being good at sport, so you actually win. But the other side is that you do it honourably and fairly," he said. "Many Australians would see themselves as above all that. That is: cheating is what other teams get up to... not the nation of good sports." He said the revelation was a "nasty shock" which brought the country "collective shame" which lingers today. He says he doubts that the cricket scene would be able to move on without a fresh response from the governing body, Cricket Australia. "One of the best ways to fuel conspiracy theories and keep sandpapergate going is to essentially say 'there's no more to see here' - especially when that comes from the authorities," Rowe said. Asked about a fresh investigation, Cummins said it was a matter for Cricket Australia. Over the marathon press conference - which one reporter suggested was the longest in Australian sporting history - Cummins was cautious, pausing often to consider his responses and to make sure they answered the questions being asked of him. But he was also frank - using strong words to reject what he said were "vague" claims by Khawaja and admitting he was frustrated a friend had put him in this position. "Friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations... That's something I've been grappling with the last couple of days." As the reporters ran out of steam, Cummins said it was "annoying" that sandpapergate scandal was still a distraction for Australian cricket. He gestured outside to the Sheffield Shield match and mentioned Friday's one-day international against England in Perth, from which he and other key players are being rested. "It's been eight years... Hopefully today we put a line through it and we're done and we can all move on to much more fun topics, like actual cricket." Few people think he'll get his wish. "It's going to be hard to move on, given that there's two sides of the story and it doesn't look like either side is going to back down," James said. "I don't know what the outcome will be." news.title: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
news.summary: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.

news.titleTr: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
news.summaryTr: Hall has been seeking a US visa in South Africa as other African beauty queens face similar hurdles.
news.articleText: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite - Published Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall and several other contestants from Africa could miss this year's competition in Puerto Rico as they race to secure a US visa. Hall is due to represent Zimbabwe at the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, with the winner set to be crowned on 24 November. But she has yet to obtain a visa to travel to the US territory. "We have been back and forth, trying to get my visa approved," Hall said in a video posted on her Instagram page. Hall is not the only African contestant to be affected by the restrictions. Zambia has withdrawn its representative, Pamela Mubanga, from the competition because of US travel restrictions. Contestants began arriving in Puerto Rico on 8 November for registration, fittings and other pre-pageant activities, putting pressure on Hall, and others including the representative from South Sudan, to secure their visas. "Officially, today is the day I was supposed to be leaving for Puerto Rico for the 75th edition of Miss Universe," Hall said. Zimbabwe is among 19 countries subject to partial US travel restrictions introduced under the Presidential Proclamation 10998, which took effect on 1 January 2026. The measures suspend the issuance of visitor, student and exchange visas, as well as immigrant visas, to nationals of the affected countries. They also impose restrictions on other categories of non-immigrant visas. In a statement, the Miss Universe organization in Zambia said Mubanga's situation was a consequence of the travel restrictions rather than individual circumstances. "Unlike situations where a contestant's visa is denied due to personal circumstances, documentation or organisational challenges, Mubanga's situation is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction affecting Zambia and other African countries," the statement read. Mubanga, 25, a registered nurse, was crowned Miss Universe Zambia on 8 October and was due to represent the country at the international pageant. The statement said five other African countries faced similar difficulties, although it did not name them. Hall said she shared their concerns, adding that she had spent the past few weeks in South Africa trying to secure her visa. "I am not alone in this predicament. Some of my African sisters are facing the same predicament, and I know exactly what they are going through," she said. Miss Universe South Sudan also expressed uncertainty about her participation, commenting on Hall's video: "It is 50/50 whether we will make it, Miss Universe." In another video posted three days earlier, Hall said she was still hoping to make it to Puerto Rico. She captioned the video: "The fight to get Zimbabwe to Puerto Rico continues," The pageant's final is scheduled to take place at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan. news.title: Politicians back focus on cost of living
news.summary: The Government of Jersey's key priorities are passed despite concerns over a lack of "real action".

news.titleTr: Politicians back focus on cost of living
news.summaryTr: The Government of Jersey's key priorities are passed despite concerns over a lack of "real action".
news.articleText: Politicians back focus on cost of living - Published Politicians have backed the Government of Jersey's key priorities for the next political term which includes action on the cost of living. States members adopted the Common Strategic Policy, external which lays out the Council of Ministers' priorities for the political term until 2030. The priorities are centered around four pillars including targeted action on the cost of living, restoring Jersey's competitiveness, investing in homes and infrastructure and maintaining financial stability. Chief Minister Lyndon Farnham said the government was determined "to make Jersey a more affordable place to live" but Reform Jersey co-leader Lyndsay Feltham said the policy lacked "real action". The policy was backed with 31 votes in favour, 10 against and two abstentions. Ministers first published the proposed policy in September and this week politicians debated a number of amendments proposed by backbenchers. This included adding a priority about government transparency and promoting democracy, bringing the total number of priorities up from 11 to 12. Deputy Feltham's amendments to add actions to the policy about household affordability and employment rights were rejected and members also voted not to include reference to rental stress. The Reform Jersey co-leader said she was worried about the gaps this left behind. "What I really wanted to see from government was something more sustained and a sustained commitment to reduce everyday cost of living," said Feltham. "They've committed to a review of household affordability. A review doesn't put food on the table or a roof over somebody's head. "I am really concerned that ministers aren't going to actually take any action." However, the chief minister said the policy recognised islanders' concerns such as affordability, housing, economic growth, investing in infrastructure and protecting the environment. In his closing speech, Farnham said their contributions "reflected a shared commitment to securing the best possible future for our island". He said the policy "will send an important message to islanders that we are putting their interests before our political disagreements". news.title: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow
news.summary: Producers claimed without more support, they could be forced to stop using British-grown apples.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow
news.summaryTr: Producers claimed without more support, they could be forced to stop using British-grown apples.
news.articleText: Cider makers fear future for orchards as costs grow - Published Rising costs could force the cider industry to reduce their reliance on British-grown apples, according to several well-established businesses. Higher alcohol duty, energy bills and packaging costs are making it harder to stay profitable, according to a producer in Somerset. The government said it was supporting the sector by increasing the value of Small Producer Relief, which provides lower alcohol duty rates for some smaller and medium-sized producers. Matilda Temperley, director of Burrow Hill farm near Martock, said it would be a "tragedy" to stop using its own apples due to climbing costs. Temperley, whose farm has been growing apples for 300 years, said recent increases had added to pressures already facing the industry, adding at 6% alcohol, their traditional cider is taxed at a higher rate than mass produced cider. More from Somerset - Christmas market fears as roadworks cause long delays - Published6 hours ago - Gritters out for the first time this autumn - Published20 hours ago - No radical change after nationalisation, GWR says - Published16 hours ago "By next February, we will have seen a 61% increase in tax on our standard 50cl bottles," Temperley claimed. She welcomed the rise in Small Producers Relief but said other mounting costs outweighed it. "We've got huge, energy costs, then almost a 90% increase in tax costs since 2020." "The thing that will happen is that if you're a big cider maker, you're going to look to cut your costs and the only way to cut costs is to stop using British apples," she said. "That's a real tragedy because cider should be made from these beautiful orchards". Isaac Stell, a financial analyst at Wealth Club in Bristol, said that having pledged not to raise the main rates of income tax, national insurance or VAT for working people, the recent budget focused on other areas to "help plug the fiscal hole." He said producers were also dealing with higher employer National Insurance contributions and increases in the minimum wage. "Inevitably, some of those additional costs will find their way through to the pubs, clubs and restaurants that producers supply, and ultimately to an already squeezed consumer. " The Showerings family, known for producing Babycham, has been making drinks in Shepton Mallet for more than 14 generations. "Our business has grown a lot in the last ten years - we've gone from having 80 employees to around 350 now," the firm's managing director Matthew Showering said. "We've had a good couple of years, we're making drinks that are popular and growing." While acknowledging rising costs, Showering said he would rather see less government intervention. "We don't want any help from the government, we'd rather they keep out of things as much as possible." Matt Gillett from Tricky's Cider in Low Ham said the size of his operation means he will be eligible for the Small Producer Relief but adds he will not see a huge benefit as the Alcohol Duty is a "fairly substantial" part of his monthly outgoings. Gillett remains optimistic, and said he would not consider importing pulp or concentrate to cut costs. "We are a craft producer here in Somerset and are proud of the fact we take from local orchards, traditional orchards, and use the fruit that is available here in this county." A spokesperson for the Treasury said: "The cider industry makes a vital contribution to our rural economy and communities, and cider continues to benefit from significantly lower duty rates than other alcoholic drinks. "But we know the industry is facing continued pressures, which is why the Budget provides additional support by cutting costs for pubs and bars that are vital customers for the industry and poured pints continue to benefit from draught relief." news.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, US President Donald Trump nominated four new SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for prominent crypto advocate Hester Peirce; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang abruptly resigned as the chipmaker’s shares plunged and a Coinbase executive warned that proposed EU restrictions on decentralized finance could push users toward riskier platforms. Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and CEO and stepped down from the company’s board on Thursday, effective immediately. The board named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO. Kress will retain her role as CFO while Nvidia’s board considers internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO role. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones its first chair and said it expects Nvidia’s operations to proceed without interruption. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance. Bitcoin (BTC) fell alongside Nvidia shares, dropping as much as 3.5% to a multimonth low. The shares later pared losses to trade at $165 at 4:24 p.m. UTC, down 5% on the day. The stock was down more than 26% over the previous month. EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec European Union efforts to tighten oversight of decentralized finance (DeFi) could drive crypto users toward platforms offering fewer investor protections, according to Coinbase’s head of EU policy. Roeland Van der Stappen told Cointelegraph that regulated crypto platforms could respond by limiting or dropping access to DeFi services. “Rules designed to protect investors would end up pushing activity towards the places with the least protection,” Van der Stappen said. In its September response to the European Commission’s consultation on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), the European Securities and Markets Authority recommended creating a new category of regulated crypto services for firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols.

news.titleTr: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
news.summaryTr: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
news.articleText: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy - Published Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December. Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines. Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X. "The American people deserve answers," he added. Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony. Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December. - How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions - Published19 hours ago - The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published19 hours ago Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China. A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang. On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive. Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing. Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday. According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company. Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close. - Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently? - Published21 hours ago Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort". One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company. It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said. Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public. Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared. Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information. The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures. Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming. But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data. Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO. Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires. news.summary: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.

news.titleTr: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
news.summaryTr: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
news.articleText: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say - Published Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision. Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her". John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed". They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said. "My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said. Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me". "To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued. The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision". "The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said. Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better". He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time". In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

news.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

news.titleTr: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
news.summaryTr: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.
news.articleText: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI - Published State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say. More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau. "The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman. This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company. US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim. Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software. According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet. Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction. A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims. Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities. The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user". "It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday. "If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation

news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-
